appearances.session: Scientific Protocols: the Making and Breaking of Scientific Norms
appearances.eventFull: Philosophy of Science Association, 30th Biennial Meeting (Area: General Philosophy of Science), in person
appearances.description: An in-person symposium on scientific protocols as the standardized, explicit procedures behind knowledge production and evidence-based policy, from laboratory instructions to disease diagnostics and community engagement. It asks how protocols turn abstract norms into specific instructions, what their virtues and limits are as norms caught between stability and variability, and what kind of entities protocols are. The talks connect protocols to reproducibility and epistemic justice, and make the case for doing philosophy of science from concrete protocol practice.

talks.title: Developing Protocols for Explanatory Modeling and Measuring: Insights from the Practice of In Vitro Reconstitution
Protocol Variation and the Methodological Principle of Invariance
The Non-Epistemic Dimension of Scientific Protocols
talks.speakers: Daan Kenis (University of Antwerp) and Federica Bocchi (University of Copenhagen)

appearances.session: The Life of Protocols in the Life Sciences
appearances.eventFull: International Society for the History, Philosophy, and Social Studies of Biology, biennial meeting
appearances.description: A 90-minute session built as a transdisciplinary "trialogue" across three worlds that rarely share a room: academic studies of scientific practice, applied agricultural biology, and decentralized science infrastructure. Its aims were both critical, on the ethics and technics of protocol use, and constructive, on what protocol design could become in other digital formats. Co-chaired with Hans-Jörg Rheinberger (MPIWG), run as a Diverse Format Session as part of the PHIL_OS project, and entered for the Interdisciplinary Organized Session Prize.

talks.title: Non-Standard Non-Operating Procedures: How Scientific Protocols Change (And How They Change Science)
Cultivating Standardization: The Role of Protocols in Agricultural Research and Practice
talks.speakers: Thiresia Teresa Tzatzani, Georgios Psarras (ELGO-DIMITRA) and Fotis Tsiroukis (TUM)

talks.title: Should Agricultural Data Be Cultivated Like Crops or Harvested for Compliance?
